extracted.intended_audience: CJR-X participants and collaborators (hospitals, health systems, ACOs, PGPs, collaboration agents), and their compliance/finance/data teams
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements governing reconciliation calculations, payment/repayment determination, data sharing, and permitted financial/sharing/distribution arrangements under the CJR-X model. Covers eligibility, documentation, methodology, caps, and compliance obligations for participants and collaborators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composite quality score tiers and discount factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines categories of composite quality scores and associated discount factors for CJR-X participants: excellent (>=17.1) -> 0.0 discount; good (>=12.1 and <=17.0) -> 1.0 discount; acceptable (>=6.1 and <=12.0) -> 2.0 discount; below acceptable (<=6.0) -> 2.0 discount and ineligible for reconciliation payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in applying discounts to reconciliation payments or eligibility as specified in §512.650(c) and §512.650(d); reference to §512.645 for composite quality score rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconciliation timing and general process
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS performs reconciliation calculations six months after the end of each performance year to establish reconciliation payments or repayment amounts for each CJR-X participant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For participants that reorganize under another CCN, CMS performs separate reconciliations for predecessor vs. new/surviving participants depending on whether the anchor admission/procedure occurred before or after the reorganization effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of performance year spending (claims data availability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance year spending for each episode is determined using claims data that is available six months after the end of the performance year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Episodes canceled under §512.630(b) are excluded from performance year spending calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-cost outlier cap application
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS calculates and applies the high-cost outlier cap to performance year episode spending by applying the calculation described in §512.640(b)(4) to each MS-DRG/HCPCS episode type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to performance year episode spending prior to aggregation in NPRA calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustments to preliminary target prices
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS applies the adjustments specified in §512.645 to preliminary target prices computed under §512.640 to calculate reconciliation target prices for each MS-DRG/HCPCS episode type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reconciliation target prices are the adjusted targets used in aggregation and NPRA calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation of reconciliation target prices and spending
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS aggregates reconciliation target prices for all included episodes and aggregates adjusted performance year spending amounts, then subtracts spending from aggregated reconciliation target prices to compute the preliminary NPRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregation excludes canceled episodes under §512.630(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stop-loss (limitation on loss) and stop-gain (limitation on gain) limits
rubrics_metrics.description: For CJR-X participants the repayment or reconciliation payment for a performance year cannot exceed 20 percent of the aggregated reconciliation target price amount for that performance year (post-episode spending amount not subject to loss limitation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These caps are applied after computing the aggregate difference between target prices and spending per §512.650(c)(6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional limitation on loss for certain hospitals
rubrics_metrics.description: Repayment amount for Medicare-dependent small rural hospitals (MDH), rural hospitals, safety net hospitals, and sole community hospitals (SCH) cannot exceed 5 percent of the aggregated reconciliation target price amount for the performance year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an additional, smaller cap for specified hospital types as defined in §512.605.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-episode spending adjustment (3 standard deviations rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a participant's average post-episode spending for the performance year is greater than 3 standard deviations above the regional average post-episode spending, the amount exceeding 3 standard deviations is subtracted from the NPRA for that performance year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-episode spending adjustment is calculated per §512.650(c)(7) and is not subject to stop-loss/stop-gain limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positive/negative NPRA payment consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If calculated NPRA is positive (and participant is not below acceptable quality score), the CJR-X participant is owed a reconciliation payment paid in one lump sum by CMS; if NPRA is negative, the participant owes that amount as a repayment to CMS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants with below acceptable composite quality scores (per §512.645(h)) are excluded from receiving reconciliation payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: CJR-X reconciliation report contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Each participant's reconciliation report must contain: total performance year spending; reconciliation target prices; reconciliation amount; composite quality score; quality-adjusted reconciliation amount; applicable stop-loss/stop-gain limits; NPRA; post-episode spending amount (if applicable); amount of any reconciliation payment owed or repayment owed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to notify participants and starts timelines for appeals/notice of calculation error processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proration of services that extend beyond an episode — general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS prorates payments for services that extend beyond an episode so only portions furnished during the episode are included in episode payment calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proration applies for both baseline episode spending and performance year spending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proration method for non-IPPS inpatient services
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-IPPS inpatient services extending beyond an episode are prorated according to the percentage of the actual length of stay (in days) that falls within the episode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in baseline and performance year spending calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proration method for home health agency services
rubrics_metrics.description: Home health agency services paid under the Medicare prospective payment system that extend beyond the episode are prorated by the percentage of billable service days occurring during the episode (from first to last billable service date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures only days within episode count toward episode spending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proration method for IPPS services using MS-DRG geometric mean LOS
rubrics_metrics.description: IPPS services extending beyond the episode are prorated using the MS-DRG geometric mean length of stay: first day counted as 2 days; if actual LOS during episode >= geometric mean then full MS-DRG payment is allocated to episode; if less, allocate MS-DRG payment proportionally by inpatient days within episode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any unallocated remainder is included in the post-episode spending calculation (§512.650(c)(7)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals — notice of calculation error filing deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: A CJR-X participant must submit written notice of a calculation error, in CMS-specified form and manner, within 30 days of issuance of the reconciliation report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not timely submitted, the reconciliation report is deemed final 30 days after issuance and payment/repayment proceeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals — who may file and process timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Only CJR-X participants may use the calculation error process. CMS issues an initial determination in writing within 30 days of receipt if the notice meets requirements; CMS may extend the time and may request additional information (participant must respond within 10 days) or the report is deemed final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If participant disputes the initial determination, they may invoke reconsideration under §512.190.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sharing — availability of beneficiary-identifiable claims data
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS shares certain beneficiary-identifiable claims data (raw or summarized) for CJR-X beneficiaries for baseline and performance years, subject to privacy/security laws, for participants to request for health care operations as defined at 45 CFR 164.501.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS omits information subject to 42 CFR part 2 (substance use disorder confidentiality).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sharing — request and attestation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To receive beneficiary-identifiable claims data, a CJR-X participant must annually submit a formal request specifying summary/raw data choice and attest they are a HIPAA covered entity requesting minimum necessary data and that use will be limited to permitted health care operations and not to reduce/limit care for specific beneficiaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must be in CMS-specified form and accompanied by a signed CJR-X data sharing agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum necessary data elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants must limit requests to minimum necessary Parts A and B elements, which may include: Medicare beneficiary ID, procedure code, sex, diagnosis code, claim ID, service from/to dates, provider/supplier ID, claim payment type, dates of birth/death, tax identification number, national provider identifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List is illustrative ('may include') and intended to guide minimum necessary principle under HIPAA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sharing frequency and scope for beneficiary-identifiable and regional aggregate data
rubrics_metrics.description: Beneficiary-identifiable baseline data made available annually at least one month prior to performance year; performance year data available as frequently as monthly during the year and up to six months after. Regional aggregate data (3-year baseline and performance year) also shared annually and monthly on similar schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regional aggregate data are aggregated by U.S. Census Division, summarize average episode spending, and are de-identified per 45 CFR 164.514(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: CJR-X data sharing agreement obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: A participant must sign an annual CJR-X data sharing agreement agreeing to comply with HIPAA Privacy Rule, additional CMS-specified privacy/security/breach/retention requirements, and to bind downstream business associates to identical terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Misuse or impermissible disclosure can result in ineligibility to retrieve beneficiary-identifiable data and other sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharing arrangement general rule and legal compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: A CJR-X participant may enter into a written sharing arrangement with a CJR-X collaborator to make gainsharing payments or receive alignment payments only in accordance with the section and all applicable laws (including fraud and abuse and payment/coverage requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sharing arrangements must be entered into before care is furnished under the arrangement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policies for selecting CJR-X collaborators
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants must develop, maintain, and use written policies for selecting collaborators that include criteria related to quality of care and provision of CJR-X activities and must not be based directly or indirectly on volume or value of referrals or anticipated business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A selection criterion requiring a reasonable minimum number of services is permitted if its purpose is to ensure quality of care (not to condition on referrals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharing arrangement required terms and governance oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Sharing arrangements must be written, signed, voluntary, require collaborators and their personnel to comply with CJR-X provisions and Medicare enrollment rules, require collaborators to have compliance programs, not risk beneficiary access/choice/quality, and be overseen by the participant's board or governing body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifics (purpose, obligations, effective date, financial/economic terms, methodologies) must be documented and made available to CMS upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibitions on sharing arrangements (inducement and clinical decision restriction)
rubrics_metrics.description: A sharing arrangement must not induce reduction/limitation of medically necessary services nor restrict a collaborator's ability to make decisions in the best interests of their patients (including device/supply/treatment choices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations risk noncompliance with CJR-X and fraud/abuse laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gainsharing payment source, timing, identification, and form
rubrics_metrics.description: Gainsharing payments must be derived solely from reconciliation payment amounts, internal cost savings, or both; distributed annually (no more than once per calendar year); not loans/advances/payments for referrals; and must be clearly identified as gainsharing payments when paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All gainsharing payments must be traceable (check, EFT, or other traceable cash transaction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criteria for gainsharing and alignment payments
rubrics_metrics.description: To receive gainsharing, a collaborator must meet participant-established quality-of-care criteria directly related to the episode; collaborators (other than ACO/PGP types) must have directly furnished a billable item/service during an episode attributed to the same performance year; special criteria apply for PGP/NPPGP/TGP and ACO collaborators (billing, clinical involvement, examples of acceptable clinical involvement listed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility ties payments to actual clinical involvement and episode attribution in the same performance year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal cost savings methodology requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodology for accruing, calculating, and verifying internal cost savings must be transparent, measurable, verifiable in accordance with GAAP and Government Auditing Standards, reflect actual internal cost savings from documented CJR-X activities, and must exclude savings realized by non-participants and 'paper' savings from accounting conventions or past fixed-cost investments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participant determines methodology but must meet these verifiability and exclusion requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology for determining amount of gainsharing payments
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of any gainsharing payments must be determined according to a methodology based solely on quality of care and provision of CJR-X activities, and may consider the amount of CJR-X activities provided by a collaborator relative to others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodology cannot be based on volume/value of referrals; must be administrable under GAAP and Yellow Book standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate cap on gainsharing payments derived from reconciliation amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: For a performance year, the aggregate amount of all gainsharing payments derived from reconciliation payment amounts must not exceed the amount of that year's reconciliation payment amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures distribution does not exceed reconciliation funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on conditioning payments on referrals or business volume/value
rubrics_metrics.description: No entity may condition the opportunity to make or receive gainsharing, alignment, or distribution payments directly or indirectly on the volume or value of past or anticipated referrals or business generated among participants, collaborators, agents, or affiliates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to sharing, alignment, and distribution arrangements to prevent improper inducements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions for collaborators under governmental action or integrity problems
rubrics_metrics.description: A participant must not make a gainsharing payment to a collaborator if CMS has notified the participant that the collaborator is subject to government action for noncompliance with CJR-X, fraud and abuse laws, provision of substandard care, or other program integrity problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants must check collaborator standing before distributing funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to recoup improper gainsharing payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Sharing arrangements must require recoupment of any gainsharing payment that contained funds derived from a CMS overpayment on a reconciliation payment amount or was based on submission of false or fraudulent data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation must record recoupments and explanations (e.g., overpayment or fraud).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment payment timing and form restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Alignment payments from a collaborator to a participant may be made at agreed intervals but must not be issued prior to CMS calculation of a repayment amount, must not be loans/advance/referrals, and must not be assessed by a participant in absence of a repayment amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participant must not receive any amounts under sharing arrangement that are not alignment payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate caps on alignment payments
rubrics_metrics.description: For a performance year, aggregate alignment payments received by the participant must not exceed 50 percent of the participant's repayment amount. Per-collaborator limits: non-ACO collaborators max 25% of the participant's repayment amount; ACO collaborators max 50% of the participant's repayment amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alignment payment methodologies must not directly account for volume or value of referrals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting and transaction traceability standards for gainsharing/alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: All gainsharing and alignment payments must be administered in accordance with GAAP and Government Auditing Standards and must be made by check, electronic funds transfer, or another traceable cash transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports auditability and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contemporaneous documentation and public posting requirements for sharing arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants must document sharing arrangements contemporaneously, post and update at least quarterly on a public webpage accurate current and historical lists of collaborators and written selection policies, and require collaborators to maintain contemporaneous documentation of payments (nature, parties, dates, amounts, recoupments and explanations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation must be retained and made available per §512.135.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping requirements for participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants must keep records of processes for verifying collaborator Medicare eligibility, plans to track internal cost savings, accounting systems information, description of health IT (including systems tracking reconciliation/payment amounts and internal cost savings), and plans to track gainsharing and alignment payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records must be retained and made available per §512.135 and support audits/compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution arrangements — written, voluntary, and legal compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution arrangements (when collaborators distribute gainsharing payments internally) must be written, signed, entered into before care, voluntary, require compliance with laws, and not condition participation on volume/value of referrals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective date must be included and arrangements must comply with fraud and abuse and other laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution payment methodology and eligibility conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution payments from an ACO, PGP, NPPGP, or TGP must be determined based solely on quality of care and provision of CJR-X activities (may consider amount of activities relative to others). A collaboration agent is eligible only if it furnished or billed an item/service to a CJR-X beneficiary during an episode attributed to the same performance year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Total distribution payments for a performance year cannot exceed the gainsharing payment the collaborator received for that year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution arrangement prohibitions and patient care protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution arrangements must not induce collaboration agents to reduce or limit medically necessary items and services nor reward provision of medically unnecessary items/services; collaboration agents must retain ability to make patient-centered clinical decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to all distribution arrangements and collaboration agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution arrangements — documentation and auditability
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR-X collaborators must maintain contemporaneous documentation for distribution arrangements including written agreements, dates/amounts of distribution payments, identity of recipients, and methodology/formula for determining amounts; records must be retained and made available per §512.135.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation supports compliance reviews and enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on distribution arrangements with shared sharing arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: A CJR-X collaborator may not enter into a distribution arrangement with any individual or entity that has a sharing arrangement with the same CJR-X participant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents circular/duplicative payment flows that could mask improper inducements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Downstream distribution arrangement requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Downstream distribution arrangements (when ACO participants that are PGP/NPPGP/TGP distribute payments further) must be written, signed, include effective date, entered into before care, and comply with all applicable laws including fraud and abuse laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Downstream arrangements mirror distribution arrangement requirements and must be in place prior to furnishing care under the arrangement.
